items.title: Peel launches 24/7 online virtual assistant for Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon
items.summary: If you live in Mississauga, Brampton or Caledon, there’s a good chance you have used a Peel Region service without realizing it. Peel Region is responsible for a surprisingly large number of services that residents use every day, from public health and paramedics to affordable housing, water, waste management, social services and transportation programs. Now the region is hoping to make it easier for residents to find those services with a new virtual assistant on its website. Peel Region launched the virtual assistant on Aug. 31, describing it as a digital helper designed to guide residents through the region’s programs and services and help them find the information they need. One of its biggest advantages could be accessibility. The assistant is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, in more than 30 languages, including English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese. It can also help visitors create a new My Account, which provides access to a variety of Peel Region online services, including the Affordable Transit Program, Peel Living services and water-bill payments. The technology is being introduced as part of Peel Region’s broader effort to improve its digital services, but it also highlights a longstanding source of confusion for residents: exactly what does Peel Region do?

items.title: Toronto Japanese restaurant team bringing new sushi and sake bar to Mississauga
items.summary: A new Japanese restaurant looks to be opening at one of the most exciting new developments in Mississauga. The trendy new Exchange District will be a mix of residential and retail space. Residents of this community have access to a gym, yoga room, regulation-sized half basketball court, on-site shops, restaurants, garden stations, a cold storage room, a dry sauna, a pet spa, outdoor theatre, a meditation lounge, an outdoor fitness area, a rooftop terrace, pool, hot tub, a co-working space, a party room, a sun deck, a catering kitchen and more. The development will also boast more than two million square feet of retail, shopping, dining, office and commercial spaces. Food options should include Toronto coffee shop Zaza Espresso Bar, which plans to operate “seasonal outposts” in the outdoor piazza, as well as Mediterranean restaurant Byblos. Other concepts slated to open at the Exchange district include a steakhouse, a speakeasy, a new café concept from Tim Hortons and the new and highly anticipated Japanese Fish Market. So far all that seems to be officially posted on a social media account for Japanese Fish Market appears to be some graphics promising that the restaurant will be a sushi and sake bar that promises to open soon in downtown Mississauga. If you’re a lover of raw fish and strong drinks, however, that’s probably enough to get you salivating for this new opening. ⁠ ⁠ Teasers for the new Mississauga concept advertise “Sushi & Sake Bar” and “Next Stop Sushi & Sake,” while branding takes inspiration from a traditional Japanese fish market.

The report notes the renaming of Gulleden Park, located beside Burnhamthorpe Community Centre in the Dixie/Burnhamthorpe roads area, to Ternopil Park aligns with the city’s asset-naming procedure and has so far received no objections from the public. The twinning pact between Mississauga and Ternopil, a city of some 225,000 people in western Ukraine, was struck in May. The park renaming, unanimously approved by Mississauga city council in July, also comes as a nod to what Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca described in her earlier motion as the growing and active Ukrainian community in Mississauga. Gulleden Park, as it was previously known, officially reopened on June 20 complete with a number of new amenities and upgrades. Moving forward, it will be called Ternopil Park. (Photos: City of Mississauga) Following city council’s approval on April 29 that Mississauga establish a sister-city relationship with Ternopil, the cities’ mayors signed official documents on May 15 joining the two cities “as long-term partners fostering international friendship, among other benefits,” Mississauga officials said earlier this year. The twinning agreement follows similar pacts signed between 16 other Canadian and Ukrainian cities, officials said earlier this year.

items.title: Mississauga Police Shooting That Killed 19-Year-Old Kaleym Davy Prompts Family March and Fundraising Push
items.summary: According to NOW Toronto, the family of 19-year-old Kaleym Davy is organizing a memorial march this coming weekend after he was shot and killed during an interaction with Toronto police on Delfi Road in Mississauga on August 6. The outlet reports Davy's aunt shared details of the march in a social media post, with the family asking anyone who wants to attend to contact organizers directly for the location rather than publicizing it widely. NOW Toronto reports the march comes as Davy's family continues to press for answers about the circumstances of his death and considers pursuing legal action and representation. According to the outlet, the family has also launched a GoFundMe campaign with a public goal of $45,000, while family members say their overall target is $100,000. NOW Toronto reports the funds raised are intended to cover funeral and burial costs along with legal fees, with the campaign describing the family's goal as giving Davy a proper farewell while helping them find answers and pursue justice.

items.title: Family struggles to find autism support in Mississauga school
items.summary: As parents and students prepare for the first day of school next week, a Mississauga family is struggling to find the support they need in the classroom. Roselynn Desousa said her twin daughters, Emmarose and Ava, were both diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder. Both will enter Grade 2 at St. Charles Garnier Catholic Elementary School in the fall, but Ava, who also has hearing loss, is struggling to keep up. com. ” Desousa and her husband Antonio have tried different things to help their daughter. The Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA) program was not successful. “We tried different instructors. She did not do well,” Desousa said. They have met with school officials and have been on the waiting list for the Ontario Autism Program for two and a half years. A school educational assessment determined Ava needs an educational assistant with her at school, but the board doesn’t have the funding, Desousa said. The Ministry of Education did not respond to requests for an interview, and the local trustee referred questions to the ministry.

items.title: Mississauga Lakeshore Road condo proposal scaled back to 9 storeys ahead of Sept. 8 committee vote
items.summary: The original 10-storey proposal faced two petitions with more than 2,000 signatures. A nine-storey condo building with 161 residential units is being proposed at 900 Lakeshore Rd. W. in Mississauga. This summary was produced using artificial intelligence and reviewed by an editor for accuracy and clarity. Mississauga city staff are backing a condo proposal that had drawn sharp criticism from residents. An Aug. 19 city staff report recommends approving an application to amend the official plan and the zoning bylaw to permit the development at 900 Lakeshore Rd. W. near Whittier Crescent. According to the report, the applicant made minor revisions to the proposal to address issues raised by staff, including reducing the building’s height from 10 to nine storeys. In addition, the applicant reduced the number of units from 188 to 161, increased residential parking to one space per residential unit and agreed to dedicate lands containing natural heritage features to the city. The applicant made the resubmission on March 26, 2026.

items.title: Mississauga's New Rental Licensing Bylaw Aims to Curb Renoviction-Driven Evictions
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's new Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw took effect Tuesday, aiming to stop landlords from using major repair or renovation claims as a pretext to push out tenants, a practice known as renovictions. The outlet reports city council adopted the bylaw in April after developing it with input from tenants, landlords and community groups across Mississauga. INsauga reports the rules work alongside Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act and are meant to make the eviction process clearer and fairer while reducing housing instability. According to the outlet, city officials said the changes are also intended to help protect Mississauga's supply of affordable rental housing. INsauga reports the bylaw comes after renovictions became increasingly common in the city in recent years, prompting municipal politicians to respond.

items.title: Avro Arrow returns to Malton
items.summary: A Canadian aviation icon returns to the place where it was originally designed and built. Entertainment and activities | September 1, 2026 Nearly 69 years after the Avro Arrow captured the imagination of a nation, the legendary aircraft has returned to the community where it was designed and built. Standing proudly in the new Flight Garden at Paul Coffey Park in Malton, the replica serves as a striking tribute to one of Canada’s most celebrated engineering achievements and the people whose vision, skill and determination helped make it possible. The recent unveiling marks the culmination of years of effort by Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart, the City of Mississauga, the Malton Business Improvement Area and dedicated donors who shared a common goal: creating a permanent home for this important piece of Canadian aviation history. In 1957, the first CF-105 Avro Arrow rolled out of Avro Canada’s facilities, marking an important moment in Canada’s aviation history. Designed and built in Canada, the aircraft reflected the skill, expertise and dedication of the engineers, technicians and workers behind the project. It remains one of the country’s most recognized aerospace achievements. Its history is closely connected to Mississauga. Built just a short distance from where the replica now stands, the Avro Arrow helped establish the Malton area as an important centre for aerospace manufacturing and innovation. The expertise, talent and determination behind the program laid the foundation for an industry that continues to play a significant role in the city’s economy. Today, Mississauga is home to Canada’s largest aerospace and aviation cluster, with more than 330 companies employing over 32,000 people. Over the past decade, the sector has grown by nearly 50 per cent, reinforcing the city’s position as a leader in advanced manufacturing, aviation technology, and aerospace development.

items.title: Scaled-Down Lorne Park Condo Proposal Heads to Council After Years of Resident Pushback
items.summary: According to INsauga, a scaled-down condominium proposal for 900 Lakeshore Road West in Lorne Park is heading back to city hall after years of neighbourhood opposition. The outlet reports the site sits beside Richard's Memorial Park and is currently home to a single detached house with a pool. INsauga reports the project was first pitched in 2023 as an 11-storey building with 178 units, revised in 2025 to 10 storeys and 188 units, and has now been reduced again to nine storeys with 161 units. According to the outlet, some residents have dubbed the development a cruise ship because of its bulk, and the 900 Lakeshore Committee has raised concerns over wind effects, damage to the site's Carolinian forest, added traffic, parking overflow onto parkland and groundwater management. INsauga reports the latest version goes before Mississauga's Planning and Development Committee on September 8, with a city report noting the developer would also transfer wooded portions of the property to the city.

items.title: Four Comedians Bring Nostalgia-Fuelled Gen X Humour to the Living Arts Centre This October
items.summary: According to Exclaim!, the City of Mississauga and saugaLIVE are bringing a lineup of Gen X comedians to the Living Arts Centre on October 9 for the GenX Takeover Comedy Tour. The outlet reports the night is billed as a mix of laughter, nostalgia and jokes about getting older, aimed squarely at audiences who grew up in the Gen X era. Exclaim! reports the bill features Real Slim Sherri, Kelly Manno, Dadbod Veteran (Jon Willington), Professor Nick Harrison and Justin Rupple. According to the outlet, tickets are already on sale, and fans can upgrade to a VIP package that includes a post-show meet and greet, a photo opportunity, an autographed poster and swag. Exclaim! reports a buffet dinner add-on will also be available before the show at LIVE Restaurant, located steps from the theatre, with organizers recommending reservations even though walk-ins are accepted.
